componentPlan.focusQuote: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Groups chemical bases by pairing rules to build vocabulary before studying structure

componentPlan.focusQuote: DNA is a double helix formed by base pairs attached to a sugar-phosphate backbone.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Connects nucleotides, base pairs, and backbone parts in the double helix diagram

overview.headline: DNA structure, code and copying in human cells

keyPoints.point: DNA is the hereditary material found in humans and almost all other organisms.
keyPoints.quote: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.

keyPoints.point: Genetic information is stored as a code made up of chemical bases including adenine and thymine.
keyPoints.quote: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).

keyPoints.point: DNA bases pair into units called base pairs with defined pairing partners.
keyPoints.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyPoints.point: DNA can replicate to make copies of itself so dividing cells receive an exact copy.
keyPoints.quote: An important property of DNA is that it can replicate, or make copies of itself.

keyTerms.gloss: DNA located in the cell nucleus
keyTerms.quote: Most DNA is located in the cell nucleus (where it is called nuclear DNA)

keyTerms.gloss: Small amount of DNA found in mitochondria
keyTerms.quote: but a small amount of DNA can also be found in the mitochondria (where it is called mitochondrial DNA or mtDNA).

keyTerms.gloss: Units called base pairs formed by paired bases
keyTerms.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyTerms.gloss: A base with sugar and phosphate combined together
keyTerms.quote: Together, a base, sugar, and phosphate are called a nucleotide.

keyTerms.gloss: Spiral structure formed by long strands of nucleotides
keyTerms.quote: Nucleotides are arranged in two long strands that form a spiral called a double helix.

analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains what DNA is, where it is found in cells, how bases store information and pair, how nucleotides form the double helix, and how DNA copies itself when cells divide.
analysis.subject: biology
